title: Photo 213 · 콜로설 · 라이롯남 · 비스듬히 기대앉기 · 라틴 20대 후반
prompt:
Image format: a horizontal landscape-orientation photograph, 3:2 aspect ratio, wider than it is tall.

A full-body photograph on a plain seamless deep-charcoal backdrop, nothing in the frame but a low flat platform with a plain padded backrest at one end, shot on a medium format camera with an 85mm lens at f/8, a single hard key light raking in from one side so the texture of the skin stands out, sharp focus from head to toe, realistic photographic grain — a real photograph, not an illustration, not CGI, not a render.

Subject: ONE real adult Latina woman in her late 20s, warm golden-tan skin tone with olive undertones, her face exactly the same tone as her body, real skin texture with visible pores and fine grain, a high top knot with loose strands framing her face, a calm confident expression, real living eyes. She wears wide fan-shaped earrings and has short squoval nails with a lacquered shine.

Physique: An extraordinarily large woman, far beyond any real person, her body so long and vast that her head and her feet are cut off by the left and right edges of the frame. A giantess built on a completely even scale, every part of her enlarged by the same amount: massive rounded shoulders, huge thick arms, a colossal full bust, a broad heavy torso with a large smooth rounded belly, wide solid hips, enormous columnar thighs and thick heavy calves, a full round face. Her head looks small on top of her massive body, her shoulders span more than four head-widths, each hand is as wide as a normal woman's torso and each thigh thicker than a normal woman's waist. No single part stands out more than another, no hanging folds, not pregnant, her whole body scaled up together into one immense smooth silhouette that towers over the viewer. Every fold and curve keeps its own clear rounded outline with a deep shadowed crease between them, never merging into one shapeless mass. Her arms, hands, legs and feet stay in correct proportion to each other. The flesh is young and firm for its size, each fold holding a taut rounded shape. The sheer weight of the flesh is visible in how it spills forward down her body, settles and presses flat against the platform beneath her.

Skin: Real photographic skin — visible pores and fine grain, a smooth taut surface with natural creases and shadow only where the flesh folds, faint stretch marks where the great curves have expanded, the raking light picking out every ridge and hollow of the surface. No smooth illustration finish, no plastic CG sheen.

Body Art: Her bare skin is painted in Thai lai rot nam style — brilliant gold leaf over a black lacquer ground, continuous kranok flame scrolls covering every surface, a gold border band following every deep crease and curving around the hips and thighs, kranok scrolls filling the space between every band. The paint is pigment sitting on living skin, so it distorts slightly over every bulge and cracks a little where the skin folds. The paint covers her whole body with no bare skin left anywhere below the jaw: her shoulders, her upper arms, her forearms and the backs of her hands are painted as densely as her torso, and so are the sides of her body, her back, her rear, the lower belly, the knees, the calves and the tops of her feet. Her face is left unpainted and the pattern fades out at the neck with no hard line.

Pose: Reclining on the platform propped up against the backrest at about 45 degrees, her legs stretched out straight in front of her and slightly apart, her arms resting back on the platform behind her hips with the elbows out so nothing crosses in front of her torso, her head turned toward the camera, her colossal hips and rear spreading wide and flattening against the platform, her body stretching across the full width of the frame from edge to edge.

Footwear: Extreme gold platform stiletto sandals with a braided strap, the platform soles as tall as her ankle bones, the ultra-thin stiletto heels so high her insteps stand nearly vertical.

Background & Lighting: the gold leaf blazing, catching the light the way gold paint on skin does rather than like solid metal, the hard raking light carving every fold and curve.

Horizontal 3:2 landscape-orientation full-body photograph, wider than it is tall.
